# AisleSense

AisleSense turns phone cameras into a live floor map of a store. It shows where shoppers go, how long they stay in each section, which spots block the walkway and which are just popular shelves, and which areas are truly ignored. Where the cameras cannot see well, it shades the area as "can't see" instead of calling it dead.

Built for the IIT Bombay CV hackathon, PS3 (Dwell-Time and Bottleneck Mapper), by Nikunj Kaushik, Tavish Agarwal, Snehashish Ghosh and Kavya Batra.

Every number in this file is rendered from `results/*.json` by `scripts/check_claims.py`. Each headline sits next to the baseline or trivial prior it has to beat.

## What it does

| Question a store manager asks | What AisleSense shows | Default heatmap tool |
|---|---|---|
| Which corner is dead? | DEAD only where the camera sees the floor well and visitors are far below the neighbours. Weakly seen cells are shaded UNSEEN with the tip "add or move a camera". | Bottom-decile cells, including the ones the camera barely sees |
| Is this aisle jammed? | BLOCK when people linger inside a walkway polygon while others pass. Lingering at a shelf front is BROWSE (green), never a bottleneck. | Dense, slow cells, which are mostly people browsing a good shelf |
| How long do people stay? | Section dwell from person-seconds per entry, with broken tracks merged, always next to a constant prior | A per-ID timer, which breaks every time the tracker loses someone |
| What should I change? | Plain tips, and a before/after rerun that shows which flags cleared | A heatmap image |

## Architecture

![AisleSense technical architecture, top to bottom: inputs, per-camera worker, event row, session runner, analytics, server, dashboard, offline proof](docs/architecture.png)

Read it top to bottom. Each camera worker turns pixels into floor points (YOLO11n, then ByteTrack, then the foot point through a 4-point homography). After that, only the event row `(session, cam, t, track, x, y, conf)` moves through the system, and it is the only thing stored. The ATC and synthetic sites enter as floor points directly, so they never touch the detector. The analytics rebuild per session version and are served stale-while-revalidate, so a tab switch never waits on a rebuild. The camera preview is drawn in memory with heads pixelated, and no frame is ever written to disk.

The same diagram is in [`docs/architecture.mmd`](docs/architecture.mmd) (Mermaid), and [`docs/architecture_transparent.png`](docs/architecture_transparent.png) has no background, for slides. The PNGs are drawn from [`docs/architecture.html`](docs/architecture.html); re-render both with `python scripts/render_architecture.py` (Playwright and Edge).

## Get started from a fresh clone

The repo root holds `aislesense/` (this app). Datasets, model weights and the venv live next to it and are not in git.

```
<repo>/
  aislesense/   the app (this folder)
  venv/         Python 3.11 virtual environment   (you create it)
  data/         datasets                          (scripts/get_data.py fills it)
  models/       optional YOLO weights             (otherwise downloaded on first run)
```

Needs: Python 3.11, Node 22, Git. An NVIDIA GPU is needed only for live video; the replay sites run on CPU.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/NikunjKaushik20/AisleSense.git
cd AisleSense
python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\pip install -r aislesense\requirements.lock     # includes torch for CUDA 12.4
cd aislesense
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run build
powershell -File run.ps1                                     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/ on the synthetic aisle
```

No NVIDIA GPU? Install the CPU build of torch first (`venv\Scripts\pip install torch==2.6.0`), then install the rest of `requirements.lock` without its `torch==` line.

Port 8000 busy? Add `-Port 8010`. For frontend work with hot reload, run the backend on one port and Vite on another:

```powershell
powershell -File run.ps1 -Port 8010
$env:AISLE_API_PORT = "8010"; npm --prefix frontend run dev -- --port 5180   # http://127.0.0.1:5180/
```

**Data** (needed for the `atc` and `merl_demo` sites and for the evals, not for `synth_aisle`):

```powershell
..\venv\Scripts\python scripts\get_data.py              # MERL Shopping + MOT20 labels + one ATC day
..\venv\Scripts\python scripts\get_data.py --heldout    # also the unseen ATC day (ATC part 1 archive)
```

Downloads resume when the connection drops. Licences: MERL (research licence), MOT20 (CC BY-NC-SA), ATC (research use only, cite Brscic et al.).

**Settings** (all optional): `AISLE_DATA` (data folder, default `<repo>/data`), `AISLE_MODEL` (YOLO weights, default `<repo>/models/yolo11n.pt`, else auto-download), `AISLE_PY` (Python used by `run.ps1`, default `<repo>/venv`), `AISLE_API_PORT` (backend port for the Vite dev server).

Run commands:

```powershell
powershell -File run.ps1                                   # synthetic aisle (no data needed)
powershell -File run.ps1 -Site atc -Mode replay -Speed 600 # real mall trajectories, full day at 600x
powershell -File run.ps1 -Site merl_demo                   # real store video through YOLO11n + ByteTrack
powershell -File run.ps1 -Site team                        # your phones or filmed sessions (see below)
powershell -File run.ps1 -Site synth_aisle -Headless -Seconds 20   # smoke run, no browser
```

Without PowerShell: `python run.py --site synth_aisle`.

## Sites

| Site | Data | What it is good for |
|---|---|---|
| `synth_aisle` | Labelled synthetic shoppers from `synth/` | Default dashboard, rule checks, harness proofs. Never an accuracy claim. |
| `merl_demo` | MERL Shopping clips (real overhead store video) | The CV path end to end: detection, tracking, browse time |
| `atc` | ATC shopping-mall trajectories (real, from the mall's own range sensors) | Full-day scale and the dead-zone test. These are sensor trajectories, not video, so they say nothing about our detector. |
| `team` | Your phones or your filmed sessions | Live demo and the held-out stopwatch and staged-event scoring |

## Headline results

All from `results/`. Units are stated as measured.

| Result | Ours | Baseline or prior | Data and unit | File |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blind but busy cells called DEAD | 0 of 656 (0%) | 416 of 656 (63.4%) for the decile rule | ATC, real mall tracks with a simulated weak camera; per injected cell, 10 seeds x 2 days | `atc_deadzone.json` |
| Truly ignored, well-seen cells still caught | 62.5% | 65.5% for the decile rule | same | `atc_deadzone.json` |
| Shelf browses flagged as a bottleneck | 0% | 65.8% for the density rule | Synthetic only, 120 events per kind | `synth_block.json` |
| Walkway blocks flagged | 100% | 65.8% for the density rule | Synthetic only | `synth_block.json` |
| Dwell error per visit, best swap arm | 3.83 s | 3.96 s for a constant (difference -0.13 s, 95% CI [-0.35, +0.06] s: a tie) | MOT20 train station crowd, per GT visit of at least 5 s | `swaps.json` |
| Long-stay ranking (AUROC, stays of 15 s or more) | 0.817 | 0.5 for any constant | MOT20 | `swaps.json` |
| Browse seconds per clip, best swap arm | 9.3 s | 6.5 s for a constant share | MERL, per clip over 28 test clips | `swaps.json` |
| Live throughput, one stream | 3.06x real time | | Looped MERL file, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 6GB Laptop GPU | `fps.json` |

## Honest limits

- **Dwell ties or loses to a trivial prior.** On MOT20 the best arm is 3.83 s against 3.96 s for a constant, and the 95% CI of the difference is [-0.35, +0.06] s, so it is a tie, not a win. On MERL the best arm is 9.3 s per clip against 6.5 s for a constant. On the synthetic stopwatch harness the per-ID timer is 11.5 s against 2.3 s for the prior. What dwell does beat is the long-stay ranking (0.817 AUROC against 0.5). We always print the prior next to dwell.
- **The walkway rule is proven only on synthetic data.** Block and browse results come from our own generator. The rule is frozen; it gets its real test on the team's staged footage, scored once (see the filming guide).
- **ATC is sensor trajectories, not video.** It shows the analytics at full-day scale. It is not evidence for the detector or tracker.
- **No team footage and no real phone yet.** The phone path was proven with a local MJPEG stand-in that has the same URL shape as IP Webcam. Use only as many phones as `results/fps.json` marks `demo_ok`.
- **Dense crowds.** An off-the-shelf COCO detector misses many people in packed scenes such as MOT20. Mount phones high and oblique over a normal aisle.
- **The dead-zone result is an injection test**: we simulate a weak camera or remove visitors on real tracks, then count cell calls. Real dead zones also drift: 23 of 118 of our day-1 DEAD cells were busy a week later (the decile rule: 3 of 143, mostly edge cells that stay quiet). That is why a cell that is dead only once shows as WATCH.

## Evaluation commands

Every script writes `results/<name>.json`; nothing is console-only.

```powershell
$PY = "..\venv\Scripts\python.exe"
& $PY eval/run_all.py --fast          # every result file + results/summary.json (CPU, cached tracks)
& $PY eval/atc_deadzone.py            # D-1 dead zones on ATC
& $PY eval/synth_block.py             # D-2 walkway vs density on synthetic events
& $PY eval/swaps.py --fast            # dwell swaps S1-S3 beside the prior
& $PY eval/fps.py --streams 1,2,3 --seconds 60
& $PY eval/stopwatch.py --site team       # after filming: dwell vs stopwatch, scored once
& $PY eval/staged_events.py --site team   # after filming: block recall and browse false alarms, scored once
& $PY -m pytest -q                    # all tests
& $PY scripts/check_claims.py         # every doc number against results/
```

Scored sessions are locked after one run (`var/locks/`), and a re-score after a rule change is refused on a real site.

## Privacy

Only anonymous track IDs and floor points are stored. No video frame is written to disk by default; with `record: true` in `site.yaml`, saved recordings have head regions pixelated.

## Phones as live cameras

1. Install **IP Webcam** (Android). In *Video preferences* choose 1280x720 (640x480 on weak Wi-Fi), then tap *Start server*. The camera URL is `http://<PHONE_IP>:8080/video`. **DroidCam** also works: `http://<PHONE_IP>:4747/video` (one viewer at a time).
2. Put the laptop and phones on the same Wi-Fi. If the venue isolates devices, join the laptop to a phone hotspot.
3. Mount phones above head height and oblique, looking down the aisle, never straight down. Keep them plugged in with the screen on and battery saver off.
4. Check each URL: `..\venv\Scripts\python -m aisle.ingest.probe http://<PHONE_IP>:8080/video` (prints `opened` and the frame size, or exits with an error).
5. Copy `sites/team_template/` to `sites/team/` and list the URLs under `cameras:` in `site.yaml`, with four floor marks per camera:

```yaml
cameras:
  - id: phone1
    source: http://<PHONE_IP>:8080/video
    image_points: [[100, 700], [1180, 700], [1000, 250], [280, 250]]   # 4 floor marks in the image (px)
    floor_points: [[0, 0], [6, 0], [6, 6], [0, 6]]                      # the same marks on the floor (m)
```

You can also click the four marks in the dashboard's Setup tab. Use at most as many phones as `results/fps.json` marks `demo_ok`. If a phone stops sending frames, that camera switches to replay with a red banner and goes live again when frames return.

## Filming and scoring the team session

This turns the synthetic browse and block results into real ones.

1. **Set up.** Pick a corridor with tables or shelves on one side and a free walkway beside them. Tape the walkway, a shelf-front strip about 1 m deep, and three shelf sections named `Section A`, `Section B` and `Section C`. Tape four floor marks every phone can see and measure them in metres. Draw the same zones in `sites/team/zones.geojson` (`kind`: `section`, `walkway`, `shelf_front`) or in the Setup tab.
2. **Roles.** A director calls cues, a timekeeper fills the stopwatch sheet off camera and never acts, and the rest are shoppers.
3. **Record files as well as streaming.** Record on each phone at 1280x720 and copy the files to `<repo>/footage/` (not in git), for example `s1_phone1.mp4` and `s2_phone1.mp4`. Point `sites/team/sessions.yaml` at them (`tune: [s1]`, `score: [s2]`).
4. **Sync.** At the start of every recording the director claps once in view of all phones while the timekeeper starts the stopwatch. The clap's time in each video is the offset to add to stopwatch times.
5. **Freeze the rules before filming.** A shopper is in a section when both feet are inside its tape. A **block** is people standing in the walkway tape while passers slow down or step around them. A **browse** is people standing in the shelf-front strip while the walkway stays free. Nothing is tuned on s2.
6. **Session s1 (tuning, about 25 min):** a few dwell walks, where one shopper visits two or three sections and pauses in each, plus some staged blocks and browses.
7. **Session s2 (scored once, about an hour):** more dwell walks and at least 20 blocks and 20 browses. Don't look at any s2 output until both label files are saved.
8. **Labels** go in `sites/team/labels/`, in video time:
   - `stopwatch.csv`: `session,section,person,t_in,t_out`
   - `events.csv`: `session,type,t0,t1,zone` (`type` is `block` or `browse`; names must match `zones.geojson`)
9. **Score once:** `python eval/stopwatch.py --site team`, then `python eval/staged_events.py --site team`. The first scored run locks s2. A re-run needs `--force-rescore`, which is recorded, and a re-score after a rule change is refused. Report the numbers as they come, next to the prior.

## Repo layout

| Path | What is in it |
|---|---|
| `aisle/` | The app: `cv/` (YOLO, ByteTrack, ghost hold, head blur), `geo/` (homography, floor grid), `analytics/` (dwell, dead zones, walkway vs shelf, tips), `ingest/` (video, phone, ATC and synthetic sources), `api/` (FastAPI and WebSocket), `store/` (SQLite) |
| `frontend/` | React and TypeScript dashboard (Vite) |
| `eval/` | Every evaluation; each writes `results/<name>.json` |
| `results/` | The numbers in this README |
| `sites/` | One folder per site: `site.yaml`, `zones.geojson`, sessions and labels |
| `synth/` | Synthetic shopper generator and labelled scenarios |
| `scripts/` | `get_data.py` (datasets) and `check_claims.py` (README numbers against `results/`), `render_architecture.py` (the diagram PNG) |
| `tests/` | The `pytest` suite; tests that need the datasets skip without them |
| `configs/` | Tracker settings and seeds |

The numbers in this README are rendered from `results/*.json` by `scripts/check_claims.py` on the maintainer's machine. If you change an eval and its results file, say so in your pull request so the README gets re-rendered.
